parts.label: (b)
parts.stem:
Iron is made when iron(III) oxide is heated with carbon monoxide, as shown by reaction 2.

reaction 2 $$\text{Fe}_2\text{O}_3 + 3\text{CO} \rightarrow 2\text{Fe} + 3\text{CO}_2$$

Table 4.1 shows enthalpy change of formation data measured at $298\text{ K}$ and $101\text{ kPa}$.

Table 4.1

| substance | equation | value for $\Delta H_{\text{f}}^{\ominus} / \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| $\text{Fe}_2\text{O}_3$ |  | $-824.2$ |
| $\text{CO}$ |  | $-110.5$ |
| $\text{CO}_2$ | $\text{C(s)} + \text{O}_2\text{(g)} \rightarrow \text{CO}_2\text{(g)}$ | $-393.5$ |

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text:
Complete Table 4.1 by adding equations with relevant state symbols to represent:

- standard enthalpy change of formation for $\text{Fe}_2\text{O}_3$

- standard enthalpy change of formation for $\text{CO}$.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
Use the data in Table 4.1 to calculate the enthalpy change of reaction, $\Delta H_{\text{r}}$, in $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$, for reaction 2.

Show your working.
